subject: Telemetry handoff & runbook execution plan for BlueBay SRE integration
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
To: BlueBay Analytics <eng+prod@bluebay.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry handoff & runbook execution plan for BlueBay SRE integration

Hi Samir / BlueBay team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is a draft runbook (runbook-draft-v1.md) and a CSV with the dashboard stubs we discussed. This thread will be the canonical handoff channel for telemetry + operations readiness for the integration. Quick goals for this phase: 

- Collect and validate the set of dashboards and traces we need for initial SLIs (latency p50/p95, error rate, token throughput per request).
- Ensure tracing hooks are instrumented across the gateway -> runtime -> cache boundary with consistent span names and tags.
- Wire alert routing so BlueBay on-call gets P0/P1 incidents, Redwood SRE gets P2/P3, and we have a documented runbook for escalations.

High-level acceptance criteria (suggested):
1) Dashboards populated with live data and viewable by BlueBay engineers.
2) End-to-end trace visible for a single request including model call, cache hit/miss, and token generation segments.
3) PagerDuty service for BlueBay (BB-SRE) receives P0 alerts within 60s of threshold breach.
4) Runbook steps for containment + rollback validated in a dry run.

Questions for your team:
- Who will own the BlueBay-side PagerDuty service and Slack channel? Please share PD escalation policy URL.
- Any compliance constraints on traces (PII/redaction) we should apply before telemetry is shared?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Today: BlueBay confirms PD owner and whether traces need redaction.
- Thu 6/13: Redwood engineers (Ben/Priyom) will push the tracing hook naming convention and a sample span example.
- Fri 6/14 11:00 PT: 60-minute checkpoint to validate live dashboard and run a dry-run incident. Meeting link: https://meet.google.com/gbh-redwood-bluebay

Attachments: runbook-draft-v1.md (markdown) — includes runbook sections: incident detection, triage, rollback steps, postmortem template; dashboard-links.csv — list of recommended panels; alert-routing-matrix.xlsx — proposed escalation matrix.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
aomi_feldman@redwood.example

From: Samir Patel <samir@bluebay.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
Cc: BlueBay Analytics <eng+prod@bluebay.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry handoff & runbook execution plan for BlueBay SRE integration

Thanks Naomi — good plan. Ben / Priyom, quick notes from my side: 

- PagerDuty: PD service is owned by BlueBay SRE (PD team: BB-SRE). I will share the escalation URL and the incident runbook snippet by EOD.
- Traces: We have a policy to redact user_identifiers and email fields in traces that leave our prod tenant. We can share sampling rules. Is there a preferred format you want for the redaction rules?
- Dashboard access: please add bluebay-analytics@bluebay.ai to the Redwood dashboard group so our product team can view.

A couple of clarifying asks before the dry run: 
1) When you say "end-to-end trace", do you expect a single-entry trace ID propagated from our gateway through the model invocation and back? We typically splice spans for third-party model calls.
2) For the dry-run incident, can you confirm which synthetic traffic pattern we should use (low qps spike vs long-tail latency)? We can generate both but want to align on what's most useful.

We are available for the Fri checkpoint but if possible we'd like to do a short pre-check tomorrow morning with Ben to validate span names.

Samir
Samir Patel
Lead SRE, BlueBay Analytics
samir@bluebay.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Samir Patel <samir@bluebay.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2029 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry handoff & runbook execution plan for BlueBay SRE integration

Samir / Naomi —

Thanks — short checklist from engineering for the span and alert conventions we intend to push tomorrow: 

Span naming conventions (will be added to runbook-draft-v1.md):
- redwood.request - top level request span
- redwood.model.invoke - model invocation 
- redwood.cache.lookup - prefix/KV cache hit/miss (tag: cache.status = hit|miss)
- redwood.streaming.chunk - token generation chunk spans (include token_count tag)

Required span tags (minimum):
- service.version (model identifier and model version)
- request.id (trace propagated request id)
- customer.id (redacted if PII flag set)

Example log-to-trace mapping: 
- ERROR logs that include redwood.request id will emit an error tag on the active span which triggers the alert rule.

Alert thresholds we propose for dry-run: 
- P0: error_rate > 1.0% over 30s AND p95 latency > 3s -> route to BB-SRE PD as P0 (page).
- P1: error_rate > 0.5% over 2m -> notify BB-SRE and Redwood SRE (P1).
- P2: p95 latency > 2s for 5m -> ticket to Redwood ops, cc BlueBay.

Routing: Our alert-routing-matrix.xlsx maps the PD services and Slack channels. For the Friday dry-run we will: 
1) Route simulated P0 to BB-SRE.
2) Route P1 to #bluebay-ops (Slack) and Redwood #redwood-ops.

Two implementation notes: 
- We will expose a sampling header (X-Redwood-Sample) so you can force-sample traces for low-volume requests during testing.
- Redaction: Priyom will send a redact.json config for BlueBay to review; it includes fields to remove or hash before traces are sent to any shared viewer.

Attachments updated: runbook-draft-v1.md (added span naming and alert thresholds), dashboard-links.csv (added panel IDs).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example

Subject: Re: Telemetry handoff & runbook execution plan for BlueBay SRE integration

Samir — thanks for the quick turnaround and for confirming PD ownership. A few final coordination items before our 11:00 PT dry-run tomorrow: 

1) Owners and responsibilities (who will run the step during dry-run):
   - Telemetry gating + sampling header tests: Ben Carter (Redwood)
   - Trace redaction config review: Priyom Das (Redwood) + Samir (BlueBay)
   - Dashboard access + validation: Marissa Cole (Redwood) + BlueBay product lead (TBD)
   - Incident dry-run facilitator: Samir (BlueBay)

2) Meeting: Fri 6/14 11:00 PT (canonical link above). Please ensure BB-SRE PD escalation URL is accessible in case we need to escalate.

3) Pre-run checklist (please reply-all once complete):
   - [ ] BlueBay PD owner and policy link provided
   - [ ] Trace redaction requirements sent to Redwood (samir@bluebay.ai -> priom_das@redwood.example)
   - [ ] Redwood has added bluebay-analytics@bluebay.ai to dashboard viewers
   - [ ] runbook-draft-v1.md updated with span names (Ben)

If everyone confirms, we'll proceed with the dry-run and mark the runbook as "validated" pending a short postmortem. Forwarding the updated runbook and dashboard CSV in the thread for reference.
